params.message: polishes his laminated name badge on a green sleeve until it squeaks.
fans a brochure at a passerby who does not slow down, and keeps smiling anyway.
calls out, "Own a piece! No charge for talk!" to the middle distance.

description: A bright, tireless man working a folding card table like it's a stage. His Franchise-green blazer is a half-size too eager and pressed within an inch of its life; a laminated badge reads DENNY CORLISS · ONBOARDING. The brochures fanned in front of him have clearly never left the table, but his smile keeps selling anyway: the practised warmth of someone who's decided, on purpose, to be the only good news on the street.

options.label: "Start me at the top. How do I found one?"
options.text: "Start me at the top. How do I found one?"

catch.text: For just a beat the smile hangs on nothing, like a coat on a hook. "Catch. Sure. Everybody wants the catch." He straightens a brochure that was already straight. "There's no catch you can *see*, and that's the honest answer. The license is real. The city's really up for grabs. It's just..." He glances up, briefly, at nothing, at everything. "They only let the good ground go where the work gets *noticed*. Push hard enough, get big enough, and you'll feel something up north start paying attention. Most folks never get far enough to find out what." The switch flips back on. "But you're not most folks, are you. So. Where do we start?"

dq_accept.text: He shakes your hand with both of his, which takes longer than a handshake should. "Welcome to the ground floor. It's the best floor. Every floor above this one is just people who miss it."

dq_cash.text: He pays you out of the float, all of it, and the float is now nothing. "Smart," he says, and means it, and it costs him something to mean it. "Genuinely. Smart." He fans the brochures back out for a street with nobody on it. "Come see me if you get bored of being smart."

dq_down_done.text: "McCracken said yes," Denny says. He says it twice more, to himself, in different tones, testing whether it is still true each time. "Nineteen months I have walked past that man." He pays you properly, from a tin, and the tin has more in it than the float ever did. "You're above somebody now. That's the part they don't warn you about. It's worse."

dq_offer.text: The smile does not change but something behind it leans forward. "Okay. Okay okay okay. You're asking, which means you're already halfway." He counts a hundred out of a float that is visibly most of what he has and puts it in front of you without letting go of it yet. "Buy something. Sell three somethings. Push eight hundred through this town in an afternoon. That's it. That's the whole ask. Franchise doesn't want proof you're good, they want proof the MODEL is good, and the model is good, kid, the model is beautiful." He lets go of the money. "Bring me the numbers."

dq_pyramid.text: "It's a STRUCTURE," he says, delighted, like you have finally said something interesting. "Everything's a structure. The Watch is a structure. The vats are a structure. You know what the difference is between a pyramid scheme and an economy?" He waits exactly long enough. "Scale. That's it. That's the only difference and everybody in a nice coat knows it." The smile comes back up like a shutter. "So. Hundred, or no hundred?"

dq_report.text:
He reads the numbers off you like a man reading a letter from home, lips moving, twice. Then he sits down on the folding chair for the first time all week.

"That works," he says quietly. "That actually works." He looks up, and the sales voice is not in it. "So here's where I have to be honest with you, and I don't get to do this much. You can take the money and walk, and it's good money, and I'll still wave at you on the street. Or you can sign, and you go on the ladder under me, and then it's not an afternoon any more."

dq_signed.text: He produces a form from somewhere in the blazer. There is a cartoon of a ladder on it and every rung is smiling. He watches you sign it with an expression that is not triumph and is not quite guilt, and hands you a cap. "Corporate identity," he says. "Don't look at me like that. Nobody picks their own."

options.label: "Alright, what else do I need to know?"
options.text: "Alright, what else do I need to know?"

found.text: He plants both palms on the table like he's been waiting all week. "Simplest thing in the world, and the hardest. You just *decide*. Type corp found <name> and pick something they'll spray on a wall someday. It runs you 1000₵ for the license, the paperwork, the *realness* of it, and the second it clears, that's it: you're the Founder. Not a packet. Not a number. A name at the top of an org chart." He taps his own badge. "First one's the whole battle, kid."

ground.text: His voice drops, conspiratorial, delighted. "*That's* the good part. A name's just a name until it's stamped on dirt. Stand in a district that matters and type corp claim, and now it's tugging your way. Some rival's already sitting on the block you want? corp contest theirs and pull it loose, inch by inch. And when you want to see the whole board, who holds what, where the lines are moving, corp map lays the city out in your colours and everyone else's." He spreads his hands like he's showing you a kingdom.

menu.text: "Course. Pick your poison." He fans the brochures again, all business, all delight.

people.text: "An outfit of one is a hobby," he says, like it's the saddest thing he's ever heard. "You want bodies. corp invite <name> puts the word out to somebody standing near you. They say yes, they're yours. Want to see who's already flying your colours? corp roster, any time. Watch it grow. There's no feeling like it." He almost means it.

options.label: "Fine. How does a person actually start one of these?"
options.text: "Fine. How does a person actually start one of these?"

options.label: "Say I had people. How do they get in?"
options.text: "Say I had people. How do they get in?"

options.label: "The posters go on about 'holding ground.' What's that mean?"
options.text: "The posters go on about 'holding ground.' What's that mean?"

options.label: "And the money? Where does it live?"
options.text: "And the money? Where does it live?"

options.label: "What would it take to actually make money at this?"
options.text: "What would it take to actually make money at this?"

root.text: A folding card table, a stack of laminated brochures nobody's touched, and behind them a man who lights up like a switch the second you slow down. Franchise-green blazer a half-size too eager, a smile focus-grouped to within an inch of its life. "There she is, fresh off the line, still got the shine on you! Don't walk past, don't walk past. Denny Corliss, Franchise onboarding, and I have got the only good news in this whole grey town." He fans a brochure he doesn't hand over. "You woke up owning nothing. I'm here to fix step one of that. Ask me anything. No charge for talk."

treasury.text: "A shared pot. That's what makes it a *corp* and not just friends," he says. "corp contribute <amount> feeds the treasury; corp disburse pays it back out when your people earn it. Territory pays rent into it, upkeep bleeds out of it, and the whole thing runs off a console." He jerks a thumb vaguely northward. "Every headquarters gets its own ops terminal, and use it when you've got one. Or, right now, anywhere: just type corp and it opens for you. Go on. Poke it. It won't bite till you've got something to lose."

clothing_layers: a too-green Franchise blazer, pressed sharp
scuffed dress shoes hidden behind the table

name: Denny Corliss
